edges.rationale: Elevated interest rates made cars less affordable, leading Tesla to implement aggressive price cuts to stimulate demand.
Aggressive price cuts directly led to a compression in profit margins and average selling prices.
Planned factory downtimes for upgrades directly caused a sequential decline in production and deliveries, leading to the miss.
Lower than expected production and deliveries contributed to Tesla missing revenue expectations.
Compressed profit margins and lower average selling prices directly resulted in Tesla missing earnings and revenue expectations.
Musk's pessimistic economic outlook during the earnings call is correlated with the earnings and revenue miss, providing context for the company's performance.
A decline in market share suggests increased competition, which could indirectly impact sales and correlate with missing revenue targets.
Strong year-over-year delivery growth partially offset the negative impacts, preventing an even larger miss on earnings and revenue.
Maintaining the annual delivery target signaled confidence and might have tempered negative market reactions, slightly inhibiting the severity of the earnings miss.
Growth in the energy business provided a diversified revenue stream, which helped to slightly mitigate the overall revenue miss from the automotive segment.
Historical DAG connected this factor to the redacted target measurement; the realized value and outcome mapping are omitted.
